title: CTR Security with a PRP
summary: A streaming bound is known for one-block messages, but extending CTR security analysis to the general PRP setting or finding a different proof remains open.

formal_statement.body: Develop a security analysis for CTR\$ when the underlying blockcipher $F$ is modeled as a PRP, beyond the one-block-message setting for which a streaming bound is available. The existing CTR\$ streaming analysis treats $F$ as a random function and relies on its entropy; when $F$ is instead a random permutation, its entropy is not sufficiently large for that argument. The unresolved task is to extend the analysis or devise a different proof for the general PRP setting.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography, focused on the security of CTR\$ mode with blockciphers.
assumptions: The underlying blockcipher $F$ is modeled as a PRP.
parameters: CTR\$ mode: the construction under analysis
Message length: beyond the one-block-message setting
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the CTR\$ security analysis to the general PRP setting or devise a different proof.

citations.label: Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption

progress.summary: The source explicitly identifies the gap: the existing CTR\$ streaming analysis handles a random function, while random-permutation entropy is insufficient for that argument. It notes a streaming bound for one-block messages and leaves extension to the general PRP setting unresolved.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption
